Each student desiring to pursue a music major at WSU must have an audition with the studio teacher of the major instrument or voice of intended study, and in the case of multiple teachers in the studio, with the area coordinator. Faculty and students are encouraged to set up an audition before the semester, use the first lesson as an audition, or use the ensemble placement audition as the audition. 

To be admitted as a major pursuing any degree in music, students must meet the following criteria:

1. Successfully audition into 300-level lessons on their major instrument or voice.
  
2. Enroll in MUS 251 and 252 or be approved to receive transfer credit by the Music Theory Area Coordinator. 

In addition, for students advancing in any of the Bachelor of Music Education degrees, the College of Education, Sport, and Human Sciences requires 2.5 GPA and C or better in each course listed for the major, minor and professional core, plus a 2.5 cumulative GPA.

Students following any teacher preparation option are required to present an acceptable senior half recital in the major performance medium. 

Students following any teacher preparation option must have a minimum GPA of 2.5 in all of the following areas: cumulative GPA, Professional Education Core with a C or better in each course, and academic major (and minor if any) with a C or better in each course. Students must also be admitted into the College of Education, Sport, and Human Sciences. 

Requirements include: pass the piano proficiency exam, second-year assessment, achieve a cumulative 2.5 GPA and a grade of C or better in all music classes, and a 2.5 GPA and a grade of C or better in all College of Education, Sport, and Human Sciences Professional Core courses. A solo half-recital is required. Class piano credits are not required for the degree. Students are expected to perform in a large ensemble on their major instrument during each semester of applied lessons. Additional ensemble requirements are clarified below. Any exceptions must be arranged with the instructor of the applied lessons.

This option provides teacher certification in designated arts: music (choral, instrumental, and general). 7 credits required from MUS 434, 435 (guitar ensemble only), 436, 437, 438, 441 for instrumentalists or MUS 429, 430, 431, 432 for vocalists on the student’s major instrument and at least one credit of MUS 435 or 428.

Instrumentalists must complete 4 credits in vocal performance studies (MUS 319 and/or ensemble) and vocalists must complete 4 credits of instrumental performance studies (MUS 391 and/or ensemble). At least 2 of the additional performance credits must come from a large ensemble.

Only 9 credits of MUS courses can be used to fulfill UCORE requirements.
